Title/Titre (Eng): Applying Climate Literacy Foundations (CHC101)
Description (English/anglais):
Climate literacy for public servants means improving our ability to recognize how a changing climate affects our mandates and our ability to deliver on them. This online self-paced course provides the foundational knowledge needed to understand the science of climate change, with a focus on what a changing climate means for Canada and its citizens. Participants will learn how they can contribute to a climate-resilient, net-zero-emissions Canada and enhance their understanding of why climate literacy is an essential part of serving Canadians.
 
Topics include:
 
·      introducing the fundamentals of climate science
·      discussing climate impacts and solutions, including climate change mitigation and adaptation
·      understanding Indigenous knowledge, perspectives, and climate leadership
·      exploring governance, justice, and a shared responsibility for climate change
 
Notes:
 
After successfully completing this course, learners are invited to register for Contributing to a Net-Zero Canada (CHC102) and Adapting to a Changing Climate in Canada (CHC103) to learn more about climate change solutions and the role of public servants.
 
This course is delivered and maintained by Environment and Climate Change Canada.

Title/Titre (Eng): Contributing to a Net-Zero Canada (CHC102)
Description (English/anglais):
Canada has an ambitious yet achievable roadmap to reducing greenhouse gas emissions nationwide, joining over 120 countries in committing to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050. This online self-paced course introduces Canada's Net-Zero Challenge, while exploring how public servants are critical to supporting this whole-of-society transition. Participants will explore the science underpinning Canada's net-zero emissions target and expand their knowledge of the policies designed to achieve it.
 
Topics include:
 
·      explaining why climate mitigation matters for Canadians and the federal public service
·      identifying energy systems and sources of Canadian greenhouse gas emissions
·      exploring climate mitigation policy through examples of practical solutions for different sectors
·      examining the role of public servants in contributing to the Net-Zero Challenge
 
Notes:
 
Applying Climate Literacy Foundations (CHC101) is a prerequisite for this course.
 
Learners are also invited to register for Adapting to a Changing Climate in Canada (CHC103) to learn more about the role of climate change adaptation in building a climate-resilient, net-zero Canada.
 
This course is delivered and maintained by Environment and Climate Change Canada.

Title/Titre (Eng): Adapting to Climate Change in Canada (CHC103)
Description (English/anglais): Canada is experiencing record-breaking climate events, with wide-ranging impacts on nature, people and the economy highlighting the urgent need to adapt to our changing climate. This online self-paced course explains the topics of climate change adaptation and resilience through practical examples that are relevant to public servants. Participants will learn why adapting to climate change is essential for building resilient communities and a strong economy while striving for net-zero emissions in Canada.   Topics include:   ·      explaining why climate change adaptation matters for Canadians and the federal public service ·      exploring the relationship between climate change mitigation and adaptation ·      reviewing case studies and other examples of adaptation in practice ·      examining the role of public servants in building climate resilience   Notes:   Applying Climate Literacy Foundations (CHC101) is a prerequisite for this course.   Learners are also invited to register for Contributing to a Net-Zero Canada (CHC102) to learn more about the role of climate change mitigation in building a climate-resilient, net-zero Canada.   This course is delivered and maintained by Environment and Climate Change Canada.
EN - Short description: This online self-paced course explains the topics of climate change adaptation and resilience through practical examples that are relevant to public servants. Participants will learn why adapting to climate change is essential for building resilient communities and a strong economy while striving for net-zero emissions in Canada.
Title/Titre (Fra): S'adapter aux changements climatiques au Canada (CHC103)
Description (French/français): Il se produit au Canada des phénomènes météorologiques sans précédent, ayant d'importantes répercussions sur la nature, les gens et l'économie, ce qui fait ressortir le besoin urgent de nous adapter aux changements que subit notre climat. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre porte sur les thèmes de l'adaptation et de la résilience dans le contexte des changements climatiques, illustrés à l'aide d'exemples pratiques pertinents pour les fonctionnaires. Les participants apprendront pourquoi il est essentiel de nous adapter aux changements climatiques pour créer des collectivités résilientes et une économie forte, tout en visant la carboneutralité au Canada.   Sujets traités :   ·      expliquer pourquoi l'adaptation aux changements climatiques est importante pour la population canadienne et la fonction publique fédérale; ·      explorer la relation entre l'atténuation des changements climatiques et l'adaptation à ces changements; ·      examiner des études de cas et d'autres exemples d'adaptation mise en pratique; ·      examiner le rôle des fonctionnaires dans le renforcement de la résilience face au changement climatique.   Remarques :   Appliquer les principes de la lutte contre les changements climatiques (CHC101) est un préalable de ce cours. Les apprenants sont également invités à s'inscrire au cours Aider le Canada à atteindre la carboneutralité (CHC102) pour en apprendre davantage sur le rôle de l'atténuation des changements climatiques dans la création d'un Canada dans la création d'un Canada carboneutre et résilient face aux changements climatiques.   Ce cours est offert et maintenu par Environnement et Changement climatique Canada.

Title/Titre (Eng): Introduction to Intellectual Property in the Public Sector (CHC104)
Description (English/anglais):
Considering matters of intellectual property is an important part of the decision-making process for public servants at all levels. This online self-paced course imparts the essential knowledge needed to understand, identify and apply intellectual property (IP) considerations and best practices at work. Participants will learn about the different types of IP and their roles in managing or addressing IP in a way that optimizes outcomes and benefits for Canada and Canadians.

Topics include:

•	defining what IP is and why it is important

•	distinguishing between formal and informal IP rights

•	identifying IP considerations unique to the public service

•	learning about confidentiality and disclosure

•	reviewing commercialization and licensing

Notes:

This course is delivered and maintained by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada.

Title/Titre (Eng): Fundamentals of Job Classification (CHC105)
Description (English/anglais):
Understanding the legislative and policy framework related to workplace organization and classification is an essential first step to providing guidance, and making informed decisions about classification. This online self-paced course provides an overview of the organization and classification framework of the core public administration of the Government of Canada, and explains how it fits into the Policy on People Management. Participants will explore concepts that will enable them to fully understand the inner workings of the federal Classification Program.

Topics include:

•	examining the occupational group structure

•	identifying the documents required in the analysis process

•	introducing the classification decision process and its potential impacts

•	identifying stakeholders in organization and classification and their roles and responsibilities

•	presenting the legislative and governance foundations of the Classification Program, and the powers emanating therefrom

Notes:

This course fulfills the first part of the mandatory learning program for human resources advisors seeking accreditation in organization and classification. The program includes CHC106, CHC107 and CHC108 (under development), for which CHC105 is a prerequisite.
This course is delivered and maintained by Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat.

Title/Titre (Eng): Performing Classifications Actions (CHC106)
Description (English/anglais):
The Directive on Classification provides flexibility to organizations by enabling individuals who are not accredited and sub-delegated in classification to process and approve classification actions. This online self-paced course explores classification actions that are common to organizational design and classification professionals, and provides the foundational knowledge needed to perform these actions. Participants will be guided through several practical scenarios, including how to create, change and delete positions within their organization.
 
Topics include:
 
·      creating a position using a standardized job description
·      changing the reporting relationship of a position
·      changing the title of a position
·      deleting a position
 
Notes:
 
This course is mandatory and must be taken before individuals can exercise Section 4.4 of the Directive on Classification. Persons trained in organizational design and classification must be authorized to exercise these responsibilities through a formal mechanism established by their organization.
 
This course is also part of the mandatory learning curriculum for human resources advisors seeking an accreditation in organizational design and classification.

This course is delivered and maintained by Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat.

Title/Titre (Eng): Media Monitoring in the Public Service: Application (CHC110)
Description (English/anglais):
Government departments and agencies are required to monitor the public environment in accordance with federal policies. This online self-paced course explains the requirements of the Policy on Communications and Federal Identity, as well as the role of the Copyright Media Clearance Program in detecting and tracking emerging media trends and issues. Participants will learn about their specific roles and responsibilities towards media monitoring, how to comply with copyright rules, and how to access online news, magazines, newswires, transcripts and more.

 

Topics include:

 

·         reinforcing the importance of media monitoring

·         reviewing the intricacies of journalism and copyright

·         explaining the role of the Copyright Media Clearance Program

·         using NewsDesk as an electronic media monitoring system

 

Notes:

 

This course is delivered and maintained by Public Services and Procurement Canada.

 

To learn more about the foundations of media monitoring, please refer to Media Monitoring in the Public Service: Knowledge (CHC119).

Title/Titre (Eng): Advanced Green Procurement (CHC111)
Description (English/anglais):
Procurement practitioners play a crucial role in contributing to and delivering on Canada’s Greening Government Strategy and the wider Federal Sustainable Development Strategy. This course bridges theory into practice by examining the role of procurement officers and their ability to develop strategic approaches. This course incorporates green and other complex socio-economic considerations into government contracts supporting Program Delivery to Canadians.


Topics include:


·         Understanding the Circular Economy and its elements

·         The roles of key stakeholders and their responsibilities in greening initiatives

·         Sourcing greener goods, services, and suppliers

·         Identifying risks and opportunities associated with Green Procurement

·         Applying Green Procurement strategies to the acquisition of goods and services

Developing evaluation criteria for Green Procurement

Ce cours fait le lien entre la théorie et la pratique en examinant le rôle des agents et agentes d’approvisionnement et leur capacité d’élaborer des approches stratégiques. ·         La compréhension de l’économie circulaire et de ses éléments

·         Les rôles des principales parties prenantes et leurs responsabilités dans les initiatives d’écologisation

·         L’approvisionnement en biens, services et fournisseurs plus écologiques

·         La détermination des opportunités et des risques liés aux achats écologiques

·         L’utilisation de stratégies d’achats écologiques dans l’acquisition de biens et de services

·         L’élaboration de critères d’évaluation pour les achats écologiques

Title/Titre (Eng): Halting and Reversing Biodiversity Loss in Canada (CHC112)
Description (English/anglais):
Nature is an intrinsic part of Canada's national identity, yet its biodiversity is declining faster than at any time in history. This online self-paced course explores the relevance of nature for Canadians and the impacts of biodiversity loss and its two-way relationship with climate change. Participants will learn about the foundations of biodiversity, the contribution of nature to the Canadian identity, and practical strategies for integrating nature and biodiversity into the decision-making process.

 

Topics include:

 

·         exploring the relevance of nature and biodiversity for Canadians

·         highlighting solutions to biodiversity loss and the two-way relationship between climate change and biodiversity

·         integrating Indigenous knowledge, perspectives and leadership into nature stewardship

·         exploring governance, justice and our shared responsibility towards nature

·         making data-driven decisions and engaging in research-based transformative actions for the conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity

 

Notes:

 

After successfully completing this course, learners are invited to register for Applying Climate Literacy Foundations (CHC101), Contributing to a Net-Zero Canada (CHC102), and Adapting to a Changing Climate in Canada (CHC103) to learn more about how public servants can integrate considerations about climate change and nature into their decision-making.

 

This course is delivered and maintained by Environment and Climate Change Canada.

Title/Titre (Eng): Introduction to Ethical Procurement (CHC118)
Description (English/anglais):
The Government of Canada aims to use its purchasing power to promote ethical business practices in Canada and abroad. This online self-paced course introduces the concept of ethical procurement and provides an overview of the annual reporting obligations for government institutions under the Fighting Against Forced Labour and Child Labour in Supply Chains Act. Participants will explore key tools, requirements, and resources available in the federal government to support ethical procurement practices.

 

Topics include:

·       understanding ethical procurement in the Government of Canada

·       identifying the risks of human trafficking, forced labour, and child labour in federal supply chains

·       examining Canadian legislation and international standards on human rights

·       applying requirements for ethical procurement

 

Notes:

 

This course helps procurement professionals build a general understanding of human rights risks in federal supply chains. Since it focuses on the federal procurement context, it does not cover all legal definitions or obligations. Participants should therefore continue to consult departmental authorities to ensure compliance with relevant laws, regulations, policies, and contracts.

 

This course is intended for Government of Canada procurement professionals and other employees interested in learning about ethical procurement.

Title/Titre (Eng): Basics of Staffing in the Public Service (COR111)
Description (English/anglais):
When looking to add new skills and competencies to their team, managers must first plan their staffing criteria and select the right staffing options. This online self-paced course reviews the legislative framework that governs staffing in the federal public service and explores staffing requirements, merit criteria, staffing options and other factors influencing the choice of staffing process. Participants will learn about the vision of staffing in the public service, the delegation of staffing authorities, how appointment processes are conducted, the key players involved, and how staffing interacts with the other human resources disciplines. 

Topics include: 

· staffing within the legislative framework 

· staffing strategically according to predetermined goals 

· establishing staffing and merit criteria 

· planning and executing a staffing process 

· assessing the staffing types, options and factors influencing the choice of staffing process 

Notes: 

This course is intended for human resources advisors, managers and anyone else who is interested in learning about staffing in the public service. It consists of two content modules followed by an exam, which serves to assess and validate the knowledge acquired. Participants must finish all three modules to complete this course.

Description (English/anglais):
The Public Service Employment Act makes managers responsible and accountable for their staffing. This online self-paced course provides managers with the knowledge they need to establish merit criteria, explore the staffing options available to them, and manage the candidate assessment process. Participants will learn how to choose the most effective resourcing strategies and options based on applicable legislation and policies, and about making sound decisions throughout the hiring process.

Description (English/anglais):
It is essential that managers in the federal public sector understand their roles and responsibilities towards respecting collective agreements and terms and conditions of employment. This course provides managers with a comprehensive overview of collective agreements and the terms and conditions of employment, including the information they need to correctly respond to questions about employee rights and obligations in the workplace. Participants will gain a better understanding of the day-to-day application of collective agreements and their impact on human resources management decisions.

HR practitioners play a crucial role in allowing an organization to provide strategic guidance and make informed decisions on matters of human resourcing. This online self-paced course examines the strategic role of senior HR practitioners, the different HR perspectives, and the forward-thinking skills needed to provide strategic HR guidance. Title/Titre (Eng): Inclusive Hiring Practices for a Diverse Workforce (COR120)
Description (English/anglais):
As Canada's largest employer, the Public Service of Canada has a responsibility to reflect the diversity of the Canadian people and to be representative of the people it serves. This online self-paced course presents best practices and staffing strategies for conducting an inclusive and bias-free hiring process. Participants will learn about the importance of a diverse workforce and the impact that unconscious bias and other barriers can have when recruiting new talent.

• recognizing the importance of diversity and inclusion in the federal public service
• understanding the impact of unconscious bias in the hiring process
• acknowledging potential barriers in order to attenuate or eliminate them
• identifying tools and strategies for conducting fair, inclusive and accessible staffing processes
This course is expected to launch in the late fall of 2021.

Related courses:

• Understanding Unconscious Bias (W005)
• Overcoming Your Own Unconscious Biases (W006)
• Overcoming Unconscious Bias in the Workplace (W007)

This online self-paced course presents the principles and concepts behind integrated business and human resources planning (IBHRP) in the federal public service. Effective staffing requires a plan that involves all of the stakeholders who work to respond to the human resources needs of an organization. Title/Titre (Eng): Understanding Workforce Adjustment (COR123)
Description (English/anglais):
Workforce adjustment is a situation wherein the services of an indeterminate employee are no longer required beyond a specific date. This online self-paced course provides managers and human resources specialists with an overview of the core public administration's workforce adjustment process and explains how to manage and mitigate its impacts effectively. Participants will learn how to interpret and apply the provisions in the National Joint Council's Work Force Adjustment Directive and the workforce adjustment appendices to some Government of Canada collective agreements for the core public administration.

Topics include:

- understanding the workforce adjustment appendices and the National Joint Council's Work Force Adjustment Directive
- describing the roles, responsibilities, rights and obligations of key stakeholders
- uncovering the key elements of the workforce adjustment process
- introducing the process of selecting employees for retention or layoff
- outlining career transition options for executives

Notes:

It is recommended that participants read the National Joint Council's Work Force Adjustment Directive and the workforce adjustment appendices to collective agreements for the core public administration prior to taking this course.

Title/Titre (Eng): Staffing for HR Specialists, Part 2: Planning (COR130)
Description (English/anglais):
To meet the evolving needs of hiring managers, human resources (HR) specialists must navigate through complex staffing actions, work closely with clients, and understand the distinction between requirements and considerations when making recommendations. This course (Part 2 of 3) builds on the foundational elements explained in Part 1 by examining the importance of effective planning during the staffing process. Participants will learn how to establish effective, flexible, and inclusive merit criteria, assessment plans and methods, with discretion and consideration.

Topics include:

- reviewing the legal foundations of the merit principle
- providing advice and recommendations on establishing merit criteria
- identifying, developing and reviewing efficient and inclusive assessment plans, methods, and tools
- applying the legislative and regulatory frameworks governing priority entitlements
- managing activities related to priority entitlements (registration, updates, marketing, referrals, and feedback)

Notes:

Before registering for this course, participants must first complete the following prerequisite courses, which include part 1 of this course suite:


1. Basics of Staffing in the Public Service (COR111)
2. Inclusive Hiring Practices for a Diverse Workforce (COR120)
3. Staffing for HR Specialists, Part 1: Understanding (COR129)

   \

To receive a certificate of completion for COR130, participants must attend all three virtual classroom sessions over the course of three weeks and complete the online self-paced modules before the second and third virtual instructor-led sessions:


1. Virtual instructor-led session 1 (week 1, 2.5 hours)
2. Self-paced modules 5 and 6 (approximately 10 hours of work)
3. Virtual instructor-led session 2 (week 3, 2.5 hours)
4. Virtual instructor-led session 3 (week 3, 2.5 hours)
EN - Short description: This course (Part 2 of 3) builds on the foundational elements explained in Part 1 by examining the importance of effective planning during the staffing process.

Title/Titre (Eng): Staffing for Managers, Part 2: Practical Application (COR132)
Description (English/anglais):
The Public Service Employment Act makes managers responsible and accountable for their staffing. This course presents a practical framework for exercising delegated staffing authority as a manager. Participants will be taken through various scenarios to reflect and exchange on the considerations to be taken into account during the staffing process and the implications of each.

Topics include:

·        establishing effective merit criteria

·        developing a candidate assessment strategy

·        identifying prejudices and barriers, and ways of eliminating or mitigating them

Notes:

This course is part 2 of a two-part course suite, which begins with the prerequisite Staffing for Managers, Part 1: Building on the Basics (COR112) (online self-paced), followed by Staffing for Managers, Part 2: Practical Application (COR132) (virtual instructor-led).
EN - Short description: This course provides managers with the knowledge and skills to establish merit criteria, explore the staffing options available in the public service, and manage the assessment process. Participants will learn how to choose effective resourcing strategies and options based on applicable laws and policies to allow them to meet their business needs and make sound decisions throughout the hiring process.
Title/Titre (Fra): Dotation à l'intention des gestionnaires, partie 2 : Application des principes de base (COR132)
Description (French/français):
En vertu de la Loi sur l'emploi dans la fonction publique, la responsabilité de la dotation et l'obligation d'en rendre compte incombent aux gestionnaires. Ce cours porte sur un cadre pratique pour exercer des pouvoirs délégués en matière de dotation en tant que gestionnaire. Les participants étudieront diverses mises en situation qui les amèneront à réfléchir aux considérations à prendre en compte tout au long du processus de dotation et aux implications de chacune d'elles, ainsi qu'à échanger à ce sujet.

Sujets traités :

·        établir des critères de mérite efficaces;

·        élaborer une stratégie d'évaluation des candidatures;

·        identifier les biais et les obstacles, et déterminer des moyens de les éliminer ou de les atténuer.

Remarques :

Ce cours est la deuxième partie d'un ensemble de deux cours. Les participants doivent d'abord suivre le cours préalable Dotation à l'intention des gestionnaires, partie 1 : Consolider les principes de base (COR112) (en ligne à rythme libre), puis le cours Dotation à l'intention des gestionnaires, partie 2 : Application des principes de base (COR132) (cours en classe virtuelle dirigé par un enseignant).
FR - Short description: Ce cours permet aux gestionnaires d'acquérir les connaissances et les compétences dont ils ont besoin pour établir des critères de mérite, explorer les options de dotation qui s'offrent à eux dans la fonction publique ainsi que gérer le processus d'évaluation. Les participants apprendront comment choisir des stratégies et des options efficaces de renouvellement de l'effectif en fonction des lois et des politiques applicables, ce qui leur permettra de répondre à leurs besoins opérationnels et de prendre des décisions judicieuses tout au long du processus d'embauche.

Title/Titre (Eng): Introduction to Organization and Classification (COR133)
Description (English/anglais):
As per the Directive on Classification, training is required to ensure that classification decisions are well managed and are made in the public interest. This online self-paced course is the first step in the mandatory training and accreditation of public servants working and specializing in classification. Participants will learn about the concepts of classification and organizational design, the roles and responsibilities of the main players, the scope of classification action requests, and the impacts of classification decisions and changes to organizational structure and job descriptions.

Topics include:

·       introducing classification ·       exploring organizational design ·       evaluating job descriptions ·       understanding the impacts of classification decisions

Notes:

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for first-time managers.

This course is mandatory training and must be taken by all managers who authorize organizational structures or organizational charts, approve job descriptions, and/or authorize classification action requests. All new managers who only have delegated classification responsibilities must complete this training within the first 6 months of assuming their new duties in accordance with the Directive on Mandatory Training.

This course is also mandatory for organization and classification trainees who wish to obtain their classification accreditation in order to subdelegate authority and make decisions on classification matters. The Organization and Classification Learning and Accreditation Curriculum (GCpedia) requires prerequisites for each step of the accreditation process.
EN - Short description: This online self-paced course is the first step in the mandatory training and accreditation of public servants working and specializing in classification. Participants will learn about the concepts of classification and organizational design, the roles and responsibilities of the main players, the scope of classification action requests, and the impacts of classification decisions and changes to organizational structure and job descriptions.
Title/Titre (Fra): Introduction à l'organisation et à la classification (COR133)
Description (French/français):
Conformément à la Directive sur la classification, une formation est nécessaire pour s'assurer que les décisions relatives à la classification sont bien gérées et sont prises dans l'intérêt public. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre est la première étape de la formation et de l'accréditation obligatoires des fonctionnaires travaillant et se spécialisant dans la classification. Les participants apprendront les notions de classification et de conception organisationnelle, le rôle et les responsabilités des principaux acteurs, la portée des demandes d'intervention en matière de classification et l'incidence des décisions concernant la classification et des modifications de la structure organisationnelle et des descriptions de travail.

Sujets traités :

·       explorer la classification; ·       examiner la conception organisationnelle; ·       évaluer les descriptions de travail; ·       comprendre l'incidence des décisions en matière de classification.

Remarques :

Ce cours a été jugé obligatoire par le Secrétariat du Conseil du Trésor pour les nouveaux et nouvelles gestionnaires.

Ce cours fait partie de la formation obligatoire et doit être suivi par tous les gestionnaires qui autorisent les structures organisationnelles ou les organigrammes, approuvent les descriptions d'emploi et/ou autorisent les demandes de mesure de classification. Tous les nouveaux gestionnaires qui exercent uniquement des responsabilités déléguées en matière de classification devront suivre cette formation dans les six mois suivant leur entrée en fonction, conformément à la Directive sur la formation obligatoire.

Ce cours est aussi obligatoire pour les stagiaires en organisation et classification qui souhaitent obtenir leur accréditation en classification. Celle-ci est nécessaire pour subdéléguer des pouvoirs de classification et avoir le droit de prendre des décisions de classification dans un service. Le Curriculum d'apprentissage et d'accréditation en organisation et classification (GCpédia) exige des préalables pour chaque étape du processus d'accréditation.

Title/Titre (Eng): HR-to-Pay for Managers (COR137)
Description (English/anglais):
Managers play a crucial role in making timely and accurate decisions related to human resources (HR) actions that affect employee pay. This course for managers presents realistic scenarios that explain their managerial responsibilities for respecting HR-to-pay practices and timelines. Participants will learn about the policy instruments, tools and resources in place to help them to make appropriate and informed decisions that lead to employee pay.

Topics include:

·        identifying the responsibilities, tools and processes needed to initiate pay-related actions

·        applying the appropriate acts, policies, directives, and collective agreements that support HR-to-pay decisions

·        using practical tools and job aids

Notes:

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for first-time managers.

This course is intended for managers with signing authority under section 34 of the Financial Administration Act, as well as timekeepers, supervisors and human resources specialists who complete critical tasks that impact employee pay.
EN - Short description: This course for managers presents realistic scenarios that explain their managerial responsibilities for respecting HR-to-pay practices and timelines. Participants will learn about the policy instruments, tools and resources in place to help them to make appropriate and informed decisions that lead to employee pay.
Title/Titre (Fra): RH à la paye pour les gestionnaires (COR137)
Description (French/français):
Les gestionnaires jouent un rôle crucial lorsque des décisions opportunes et éclairées doivent être prises au sujet de mesures de ressources humaines (RH) ayant une incidence sur la paye des employés. Ce cours destiné aux gestionnaires présente des mises en situation réalistes qui portent sur les responsabilités de ces derniers en ce qui concerne le respect des pratiques et des délais en matière de RH à la paye. Les participants apprendront sur les instruments de politique, les outils et les ressources dont ils disposent pour prendre des décisions judicieuses qui permettent aux employés d'être payés.

Sujets traités :

·        connaître les responsabilités, les outils et les processus permettant de prendre des mesures liées à la paye;

·        appliquer les lois, les politiques, les directives et les conventions collectives à la prise de décisions en matière de RH à la paye;

·       utiliser des outils pratiques et des outils de travail.

Remarques :

Ce cours a été jugé obligatoire par le Secrétariat du Conseil du Trésor pour les nouveaux et nouvelles gestionnaires.

Ce cours s'adresse aux gestionnaires ayant un pouvoir de signature en vertu de l'article 34 de la Loi sur la gestion des finances publiques, ainsi qu'aux responsables de la comptabilisation du temps, aux superviseurs et aux spécialistes des ressources humaines qui accomplissent des tâches essentielles ayant une incidence sur la paye des employés.

Title/Titre (Eng): Training for Learning Facilitators (COR138)
Description (English/anglais):
The Canada School of Public Service actively recruits facilitators with knowledge and experience in all aspects of public service administration. This training introduces best practices, facilitation techniques, and classroom management skills for preparing and delivering both in-person and virtual learning sessions. Participants will be presented with opportunities to observe, interact with, and learn from their peers while also engaging with an audience of learners.

 

Topics include:

- reviewing adult learning principles
- developing effective strategies for engaging learners
- practising facilitation in a virtual environment, including using a web conferencing platform
- exploring facilitation techniques and classroom management skills for traditional and virtual learning settings

 

Notes:

 

This course is offered exclusively to new learning facilitators recruited by the Canada School of Public Service.

 

The total time commitment for completing this training is about 28 hours: 15 hours of virtual-instructor-led time and 13 hours of individual self-study.

 

At the end of the training, participants will be required to prepare and deliver a sample lesson to demonstrate their facilitation, presentation, and communication skills. This will be assessed and must be successfully completed in order to pass the training.

 

For instructions on how to indicate your interest in becoming a faculty member at the Canada School of Public Service, please visit Become a faculty member.

 

Schedule:

Pre-course information session (1 week before the training start date):

- How to prepare for the training
- How to get the most out of the training
- Technical requirements

 

Pre-course activities:

Pre-course activities require about 2 hours of self-study on your own time to complete.

 

Week 1:

- Modules 1 to 4
- Introduction and Expectations
- Using a Web Conferencing Platform
- Exploring Adult Learning Principles
- Facilitating Virtually

 

Time commitment: 8 hours of mandatory virtual instructor-led training plus about 7 hours of self-study

 

Week 2:

- Modules 5 and 6
- Creating a Positive Environment
- Facilitating with Accessibility in Mind


- Optional practice sessions
- Preparing for your final evaluation

 

Time commitment: 4 hours of mandatory virtual instructor-led training, 3 hours of self-study, and about 3 hours preparation for the final evaluation; optional practice sessions and office hours are also available for additional support

 

Week 3:

- Module 7
- Final Evaluation

 

Time commitment: 3 hours minimum to complete the final evaluation; some participants may also choose to attend and observe the sample lessons their peers deliver
EN - Short description: This course, offered exclusively to new facilitators at the Canada School of Public Service, introduces best practices, facilitation techniques and classroom management skills for preparing and delivering learning activities such as courses or events.
Title/Titre (Fra): Formation destinée aux personnes facilitatrices d'apprentissage (COR138)
Description (French/français):
L’École de la fonction publique du Canada travaille activement à recruter des personnes facilitatrices ayant des connaissances et une expérience de tous les aspects de l’administration publique. Cette formation présente des pratiques exemplaires, des techniques de facilitation et des compétences de gestion de salle de classe qui permettent de préparer et d’offrir des séances en personne et en mode virtuel. Les personnes participantes pourront apprendre auprès de leurs pairs, les voir à l’œuvre et interagir avec des apprenants et apprenantes.

 

Sujets traités :

- examiner les principes de l’apprentissage chez les adultes;
- formuler des stratégies efficaces pour stimuler l’intérêt en classe;
- s’exercer à la facilitation de cours virtuels, notamment en utilisant une plateforme de webconférence;
- étudier les techniques de facilitation et de gestion de classe à utiliser dans les classes traditionnelles et virtuelles.

 

Remarques :

Ce cours est offert exclusivement aux nouvelles personnes facilitatrices de l’École de la fonction publique du Canada.

 

Au total, la formation est d’une durée d’environ 28 heures, soit 15 heures de formation virtuelle avec facilitation et 13 heures d’apprentissage individuel à rythme libre.

 

À la fin de la formation, les participants et participantes devront préparer et animer une courte séance pour mettre en évidence leurs compétences de facilitation, de présentation et de communication. Cette séance sera évaluée et sa réussite est obligatoire à l’achèvement du cours.

 

Pour savoir comment manifester votre intérêt à vous joindre au corps professoral de l’École de la fonction publique du Canada, consultez la page Devenir membre du corps professoral.

 

Horaire :

Séance d’information préalable au cours (une semaine avant le début de la formation) :

- se préparer à la formation;
- tirer pleinement profit de la formation;
- exigences en matière d’équipement.

 

Activités préalables au cours :

 

Les activités préalables au cours exigeront environ deux heures de votre temps et se font à rythme libre.

 

Semaine 1 :

- Modules 1 à 4
- Introduction et attentes
- Utilisation d’une plateforme de webconférence
- Principes de l’apprentissages chez les adultes
- Facilitation de séances virtuelles

 

Durée : Huit heures de formation virtuelle obligatoire donnée par une personne formatrice et sept heures d’apprentissage à rythme libre

 

Semaine 2 :

- Modules 5 et 6
- Création d’un environnement positif
- Facilitation axée sur l’accessibilité


- Séances facultatives de mise en pratique
- Préparation à l’évaluation finale

 

Durée : Quatre heures de formation virtuelle obligatoire donnée par une personne formatrice, trois heures d’apprentissage à rythme libre et environ trois heures de préparation à l’évaluation finale; des séances facultatives de mise en pratique seront également offertes

 

Semaine 3 :

- Module 7
- Évaluation finale

 

Durée : Trois heures minimum pour réaliser l’évaluation finale; certaines personnes pourraient aussi décider d’assister aux courtes séances de facilitation présentées par leurs pairs

Title/Titre (Eng): Authority Delegation Training: Managing People Effectively (COR152)
Description (English/anglais):
Effective people management is a critical skill in ensuring a high-performing workforce that embodies public sector values and provides good governance and service to Canadians. This online self-paced course provides managers at all levels with the basic knowledge required to exercise their delegated human resources (HR) responsibilities within the public service. Participants will acquire the foundational understanding needed to make informed and strategic human resources-related decisions

Topics include: ·        understanding the role of organization and classification in HR management ·        planning human resources and staffing responsibly ·        recognizing responsibilities related to diversity, equity and inclusion ·        managing labour relations issues ·        respecting official languages rights and responsibilities

Notes: 

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for first-time managers.

This course is part of the Authority Delegation Training (ADT) program that is mandatory for managers with delegated signing authority. Delegated managers must complete the following three ADT courses, ideally in this order:

1. Authority Delegation Training: Using Public Funds Responsibly (G380)


1. Authority Delegation Training: Practising Responsible Procurement (G381)
2. Authority Delegation Training: Managing People Effectively (G382)

These courses are also open to all public servants for professional development purposes. However, completing these courses and their assessments does not entitle these learners to exercise signing authority. Consult the Directive on Delegation of Spending and Financial Authorities for the specific responsibilities for delegating, maintaining and managing, and overseeing spending and financial authorities.

Learn more about the Authority Delegation Training Program.
EN - Short description: This online self-paced course provides managers at all levels with the basic knowledge required to exercise their delegated human resources (HR) responsibilities within the public service. Participants will acquire the foundational understanding needed to make informed and strategic human resources-related decisions
Title/Titre (Fra): Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs : Gérer les personnes de manière efficace (COR152)
Description (French/français):
La gestion efficace des personnes est une compétence essentielle pour assurer une main-d'œuvre qui offre un haut rendement, qui incarne les valeurs du secteur public et qui assure une bonne gouvernance et un bon service aux Canadiens. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre fournit aux gestionnaires de tous les niveaux les connaissances de base nécessaires pour exercer les responsabilités qui leur sont déléguées en matière de ressources humaines (RH) à la fonction publique. Les participants acquerront la compréhension fondamentale nécessaire pour prendre des décisions éclairées et stratégiques en matière de ressources humaines.

Sujets traités : ·        comprendre le rôle de l'organisation et de la classification dans la gestion des RH; ·        planifier les ressources humaines et la dotation de manière responsable; ·        reconnaître les responsabilités liées à la diversité, à l'équité et à l'inclusion; ·        gérer les questions de relations de travail; ·        respecter les droits et les responsabilités en matière de langues officielles.

Remarques : 

Ce cours a été jugé obligatoire par le Secrétariat du Conseil du Trésor pour les nouveaux et nouvelles gestionnaires.

Ce cours fait partie du programme Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs (FDP), qui est obligatoire pour les gestionnaires à qui des pouvoirs de signature ont été délégués. Ces gestionnaires doivent suivre les trois cours de la FDP, idéalement dans l'ordre suivant :

1. Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs : Utiliser les fonds publics de manière responsable (G380)


1. Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs : Pratiquer l'approvisionnement responsable (G381)
2. Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs : Gérer les personnes de manière efficace (G382)

Ces cours sont également ouverts à l'ensemble des fonctionnaires à des fins de perfectionnement professionnel. Toutefois, le fait de suivre ces cours et de passer les évaluations correspondantes ne donne en aucun cas à ces fonctionnaires le droit d'exercer un quelconque pouvoir de signature. Consultez la Directive sur la délégation des pouvoirs de dépenser et des pouvoirs financiers pour connaître les responsabilités particulières en matière de délégation, de maintien et de gestion, et de surveillance des pouvoirs de dépenser et des pouvoirs financiers.

Apprenez-en plus au sujet du Programme de formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs.

Title/Titre (Eng): Comprehending Financials: A Guide to Financial Statements (COR201)
Description (English/anglais):
Financial statements are written records that capture auditable business activities and financial performance. This online self-paced course examines three basic types of financial statements: the income statement, the cash flow statement, and the balance sheet. Participants will review the reporting requirements and arrangement of information for the different types and items of financial statements, and explore how each type relates to the others.

Topics include:

·       compiling balance sheets
·       performing common calculations
·       using cash flow statements to manage expenses
·       unpacking the essentials of income and cash flow statements

Title/Titre (Eng): Financial Statement Analysis for Non-financial Professionals (COR202)
Description (English/anglais):
A general knowledge of financial analysis is essential to understand an organization's financial standing and the financial implications of organizational activities. This online self-paced course covers different methods for analyzing financial statements from the perspective of a non-financial professional. Participants will learn about the role of common financial ratios in analyzing profitability, efficiency, liquidity and solvency, and explore different examples of horizontal analysis and vertical analysis.

Topics include:

·       understanding present value and future value calculations
·       calculating the value of key profitability ratios
·       analyzing efficiency ratios and solvency ratios
·       using percentage calculations in horizontal and vertical analyses

Title/Titre (Eng): A Tour of Internal Auditing (COR205)
Description (English/anglais):
Internal auditors help their organization to achieve its objectives by providing independent and objective assurance, and advice on risk management, internal control and governance processes. This online self-paced course for new internal auditors provides a tour of the internal audit process and how internal auditors add value to their organization. Participants will learn about internal auditing practices within their own organization and will have an opportunity to explore real-life examples of the topics covered. 

Topics include: 

· interpreting the policies and standards used in internal auditing 

· recalling the key elements in each phase of an internal auditing engagement 

· explaining internal auditing practices that are specific to each participant's organization 

· recognizing the importance of internal and external stakeholder engagement 

Notes: 

Internal Audit 101 - Myth-Busting the Internal Audit Function (GCpedia) is a prerequisite for this course. To access GCpedia, you must be connected to the internal Government of Canada Network.

Title/Titre (Eng): Applying Key Concepts in Financial Management (COR210)
Description (English/anglais):
Understanding the fundamental rules and regulations that govern financial management frameworks is an essential component of the financial curriculum. This course connects the theory covered in Key Concepts in Financial Management (COR216) with the more practical aspects of public financial management, and is mandatory training for financial officers. Through application exercises, participants will be introduced to the tools currently used to manage finances within the federal government.

Topics include:

·       using government reports in making budgetary changes ·       making changes to program budgets partway through the financial cycle ·       reviewing variance reports ·       applying a delegation of spending chart to financial processes

Notes:

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for financial officers.

This course is divided into two 3-hour sessions offered over two consecutive days.

Key Concepts in Financial Management (COR216) or Financial Management Systems (COR213) (now archived) are prerequisites and must be completed prior to registering for COR210.

Legacy course code: F304

Title/Titre (Fra): Mise en application des principaux concepts en gestion financière (COR210)
Description (French/français):
La compréhension des règles et des règlements fondamentaux qui régissent les cadres de gestion financière fait partie intégrante du programme de cours sur les finances. Ce cours obligatoire pour les agents financiers vise à faire le lien entre la théorie présentée dans le cours Principaux concepts en gestion financière (COR216) et les aspects plus pratiques de la gestion des finances publiques. Les participants se familiariseront, à l'aide d'exercices pratiques, avec les outils couramment utilisés dans la gestion financière au sein du gouvernement fédéral.

Title/Titre (Eng): Master Class on Strategic Resourcing (COR215)
Description (English/anglais):
The financial resources of the Government of Canada are safeguarded through balanced controls that enable flexibility and manage risk. This course for seasoned executives examines the principles and processes behind strategic resourcing and financial management, as well as the important role played by central agencies. Through practical workshops, participants will explore challenges, reflect on current practices and engage with colleagues to identify best practices for effectively securing the resources needed to deliver on their organizational mandate.

 

Topics include: 

- examining accountability and stewardship 


- managing finances and achieving results
- seeking authorizations and securing resources
- reporting on results and measuring performance
- advocating for proper financial resources

 

Notes: 

This course is delivered as two consecutive days of training. Registration is reserved for employees at the EX-02 and EX-03 levels. A short readiness questionnaire will be administered prior to the offering date to enable full participation in class discussions.

 

A valid Authority Delegation Validation Assessment for Executives (COR254) certificate is a required prerequisite for this course. Certifications are valid for five years.

 

Executive employees registering for COR215 are encouraged to also complete the Authority Delegation Training: Using Public Funds Responsibly (COR250) to refresh their understanding of the core principles of financial management.

 

To express your interest in participating in this course, please submit a readiness questionnaire.

This online self-paced course provides an overview of the foundational knowledge that new financial officers need to perform their role effectively. Title/Titre (Eng): Transfer Payment Basics (COR217)
Description (English/anglais):
Transfer payments make up a large part of federal government spending. This online self-paced course provides an overview of grants and contributions, including the different categories of transfer payments, the life cycle of the transfer payment program and the role of key stakeholders in the process. Participants will learn about the objectives and expected results of the Policy on Transfer Payments and its related directive, as well as the important characteristics of transfer payments.

Topics include:

· differentiating between grants and contributions

· identifying key individuals and stakeholder groups involved in transfer  payments

· examining the life cycle of the transfer payment program

Notes:

This course is part of the Grants and Contributions Learning Series.

Title/Titre (Eng): Entering into a Funding Agreement (COR219)
Description (English/anglais):
Managing transfer payment programs requires a thorough understanding of the processes leading up to the signing of a funding agreement. This online self-paced course provides a step-by-step overview of the transfer payment funding process, which includes assessing eligibility and merit, reviewing risk, making recommendations, negotiating, and signing a funding agreement. Participants will gain the knowledge and skills needed to make informed, transparent, and accountable recommendations and navigate the complexities of developing funding agreements.

 

Topics include:

·       determining the responsibilities of applicants and program officers throughout the application assessment process

·       making informed decisions on funding recommendations

·       understanding the process involved in signing a funding agreement

 

Notes:

 

This course is part of the Grants and Contributions Learning Series.

Title/Titre (Eng): Managing and Monitoring a Funding Agreement (COR220)
Description (English/anglais):
Effective management and ongoing monitoring are essential components of transfer payment programs once a funding agreement is finalized. This online self-paced course focuses on the final phases of the transfer payment program life cycle, which emphasize the importance of managing a funding agreement and a program's evaluation. Participants will learn about the responsibilities of program officers as they relate to funding agreements and will gain insights into the day-to-day operations that come into play once a funding agreement is established.

 

Topics include:

 

- understanding the reporting requirements and criteria program officers must consider before recommending payments
- implementing recipient monitoring strategies to ensure a clear understanding of funding agreements
- reassessing the risks associated with funded projects
- taking action when issues are identified during the monitoring process
- participating in transfer payment program evaluation and closing project files

 

Notes:

 

This course is included in the Grants and Contributions Learning Series.

Title/Titre (Eng): Authority Delegation Training: Using Public Funds Responsibly (COR250)
Description (English/anglais):
Managers in the federal public service are expected to have a solid understanding of the financial authorities that have been delegated to them. This online self-paced course for managers at all levels provides an overview of the expected practices for the sound management of public funds through responsible planning, spending and reporting. By reviewing helpful examples, participants will learn how to exercise their delegated financial authorities in line with government policies, practices and procedures.

Topics include:

·       developing a work plan and a budget ·       reporting on finances and results ·       exercising delegated spending and financial authorities

Notes:

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for first-time managers.

This course is part of the Authority Delegation Training (ADT) program that is mandatory for managers with delegated signing authority. Delegated managers must complete the following three ADT courses, ideally in this order:

1. Authority Delegation Training: Using Public Funds Responsibly (G380)


1. Authority Delegation Training: Practising Responsible Procurement (G381)
2. Authority Delegation Training: Managing People Effectively (G382)

These courses are also open to all public servants for professional development purposes. However, completing these courses and their assessments does not entitle these learners to exercise signing authority. Consult the Directive on Delegation of Spending and Financial Authorities for the specific responsibilities for delegating, maintaining and managing, and overseeing spending and financial authorities.

Learn more about the Authority Delegation Training Program.
EN - Short description: This online self-paced course for managers at all levels provides an overview of the expected practices for the sound management of public funds through responsible planning, spending and reporting. By reviewing helpful examples, participants will learn how to exercise their delegated financial authorities in line with government policies, practices and procedures.
Title/Titre (Fra): Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs : Utiliser les fonds publics de manière responsable (COR250)
Description (French/français):
Les gestionnaires de la fonction publique fédérale sont censés comprendre les pouvoirs financiers qui leur sont délégués. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre destiné aux gestionnaires de tous les niveaux présente un aperçu des pratiques attendues pour assurer la saine gestion des fonds publics au moyen d'une planification, d'une gestion des dépenses et d'une production de rapports responsables. Par l'étude d'exemples utiles, les participants apprendront à exercer les pouvoirs financiers qui leur sont délégués conformément aux politiques, aux pratiques et aux procédures du gouvernement.

Sujets traités :

·       élaborer un plan de travail et un budget; ·       produire des rapports sur les finances et les résultats; ·       exercer des pouvoirs financiers et de dépenser délégués.

Remarques :

Ce cours a été jugé obligatoire par le Secrétariat du Conseil du Trésor pour les nouveaux et nouvelles gestionnaires.

Ce cours fait partie du programme Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs (FDP), qui est obligatoire pour les gestionnaires à qui des pouvoirs de signature ont été délégués. Ces gestionnaires doivent suivre les trois cours de la FDP, idéalement dans l'ordre suivant :

1. Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs : Utiliser les fonds publics de manière responsable (G380)


1. Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs : Pratiquer l'approvisionnement responsable (G381)
2. Formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs : Gérer les personnes de manière efficace (G382)

Ces cours sont également ouverts à l'ensemble des fonctionnaires à des fins de perfectionnement professionnel. Toutefois, le fait de suivre ces cours et de passer les évaluations correspondantes ne donne en aucun cas à ces fonctionnaires le droit d'exercer un quelconque pouvoir de signature. Consultez la Directive sur la délégation des pouvoirs de dépenser et des pouvoirs financiers pour connaître les responsabilités particulières en matière de délégation, de maintien et de gestion, et de surveillance des pouvoirs de dépenser et des pouvoirs financiers.

Apprenez-en plus au sujet du Programme de formation sur la délégation de pouvoirs.

Participants must complete the scenarios, exercises and validation questions in their entirety to complete this assessment.

Business continuity management (BCM) programs play an integral role in assisting Government of Canada organizations to adapt and respond to evolving risks to business operations. Title/Titre (Eng): Business Continuity Management: Conducting a Business Impact Analysis (COR312)
Description (English/anglais):
To ensure the continued delivery of critical operations during emergencies, federal organizations must plan for potential service disruptions by conducting a business impact analysis (BIA). This online self-paced course explains how to conduct a BIA using the Government of Canada’s official methodology, as outlined in its Business Continuity Management Program Guide (2023). Participants will learn how to identify BIA components, communicate their value and align their work with federal business continuity management practices.

Topics Include:

·       facilitating a business impact analysis

·       identifying the diverse roles and responsibilities in the business continuity management (BCM) process

·       applying the Government of Canada’s official business impact analysis methodology

·       analyzing the criticality of services and delivery requirements

Notes:

This course offers two pathways tailored to different roles in business continuity management:

 

Pathway 1: BCM Specialist Pathway (4 hours): Designed for those leading and facilitating the BIA process as part of a BCM program. Ideal for BCM specialists and coordinators seeking in-depth knowledge of the Government of Canada’s BIA methodology and application.

·       Intended audience: BCM functional specialists and coordinators

 

Pathway 2: BIA Participant Pathway (2 hours): Designed for those contributing to the BIA process. Ideal for individuals looking to build foundational knowledge to assess the criticality of services and identify critical service delivery requirements.

·       Intended audience: Service owners, subject-matter experts, chief security officers, deputy chief security officers, individuals responsible for related resilience disciplines, general staff.
EN - Short description: This online self-paced course explains how to conduct a BIA using the Government of Canada’s official methodology, as outlined in its Business Continuity Management Program Guide (2023).
Title/Titre (Fra): La gestion de la continuité des activités : réalisation d’une analyse des incidences sur les activités (COR312)
Description (French/français):
Afin d’assurer l’exécution continue des activités essentielles en situation d’urgence, les organisations fédérales doivent se préparer à d’éventuelles perturbations des services en réalisant une analyse des incidences sur les activités (AIA). Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre explique comment effectuer une AIA selon la méthodologie officielle du gouvernement du Canada, décrite dans l’édition de 2023 du Guide du programme de gestion de la continuité des activités. Les participants apprendront à cerner les éléments d’une AIA, à communiquer leur valeur et à suivre les pratiques fédérales en matière de gestion de la continuité des activités.

Sujets traités :

·       faciliter la réalisation d’une analyse des incidences sur les activités;

·       connaître les divers rôles et responsabilités liés au processus de gestion de la continuité des activités (GCA);

·       utiliser la méthodologie officielle du gouvernement du Canada en matière d’analyse des incidences sur les activités;

·       analyser le caractère essentiel des services et les exigences liées à leur prestation.

Remarques :

Ce cours offre deux cheminements, chacun adapté à différents rôles dans la gestion de la continuité des activités.

Cheminement 1 : Spécialistes de la GCA (4 heures) : Conçu pour les personnes qui dirigent et facilitent le processus d’AIA dans le cadre d’un programme de GCA. Ce cheminement est idéal pour les spécialistes et les coordonnateurs de la GCA qui cherchent à acquérir des connaissances approfondies sur la méthodologie du gouvernement du Canada en matière d’AIA et sur son application.

·       Public cible : spécialistes fonctionnels et coordonnateurs de la GCA


Cheminement 2 : Participants à la GCA (2 heures) : Conçu pour les personnes qui contribuent au processus d’AIA. Ce cheminement est idéal pour les personnes qui cherchent à acquérir des connaissances de base en vue d’évaluer le caractère essentiel des services et de cerner les exigences en matière de prestation des services essentiels.

·       Public cible : propriétaires de services, experts en la matière, dirigeants principaux de la sécurité, dirigeants principaux adjoints de la sécurité, personnes responsables de disciplines connexes contribuant à la résilience, personnel général

In response to Canada's commitment to climate change, environmental performance is an important consideration when making procurement decisions. This online self-paced course introduces the federal government's Policy on Green Procurement and provides detailed strategies for applying its principles throughout the procurement process. ·      applying life-cycle analysis
·      defining value for money
·      evaluating environmental claims made by suppliers

Notes:

This course is open to all public servants.

Description (English/anglais):
Departments and agencies use a variety of solicitation methods to acquire goods and services through competitive contracts. This course covers two critical elements of the solicitation process: the statement of work and the evaluation criteria for bids submitted. Title/Titre (Eng): Indigenous Considerations in Procurement (COR409)
Description (English/anglais):
There are many ways contracting authorities can support economic growth for Indigenous businesses, people and communities. This online self-paced course introduces the federal procurement policies, obligations and considerations that can be applied to increase opportunities for Indigenous businesses in Canada. Participants will learn about the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB) and gain a broader understanding of modern treaties or Comprehensive Land Claims Agreements (CLCAs) and how they can affect the procurement process.

Topics include:

· determining the applicability of modern treaties/CLCAs and the key mechanisms of the PSIB

· describing the common procurement obligations that may apply when a procurement is subject to a modern treaty/CLCA

· explaining how modern treaty/CLCA obligations and the use of the PSIB may affect certain steps in the procurement process

Notes:

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for procurement specialists.
EN - Short description: This online self-paced course introduces federal procurement policies and obligations that are designed to improve business development opportunities for Indigenous Peoples. Participants will learn about the Procurement Strategy for Aboriginal Business initiative and gain a broader understanding of Comprehensive Land Claims Agreements and how they affect procurement.
Title/Titre (Fra): Considérations autochtones en matière d'approvisionnement (COR409)
Description (French/français):
Les autorités contractantes disposent de nombreux moyens pour favoriser la croissance économique des Autochtones, y compris de leurs entreprises et collectivités. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre présente les politiques et les obligations fédérales ainsi que les aspects à prendre en considération en matière d'approvisionnement afin d'accroître les occasions pour les entreprises autochtones au Canada. Les participants se familiariseront avec la Stratégie d'approvisionnement auprès des entreprises autochtones (SAEA) et acquerront une meilleure compréhension des traités modernes ou ententes sur les revendications territoriales globales (ERTG) et de leur incidence sur le processus d'approvisionnement.

Sujets traités :

· déterminer si des traités modernes/ERTG et les principaux mécanismes de la SAEA s'appliquent;

· décrire les obligations courantes qui s'appliquent lorsqu'un approvisionnement est assujetti à un traité moderne/ERTG;

· expliquer de quelle façon les obligations liées aux traités modernes/ERTG et l'application de la SAEA peuvent influer sur certaines étapes du processus d'approvisionnement.

Remarques :

Ce cours a été jugé obligatoire par le Secrétariat du Conseil du Trésor pour les spécialistes de l’approvisionnement.

Les participants se familiariseront avec la Stratégie d'approvisionnement auprès des entreprises autochtones et acquerront une meilleure compréhension des ententes sur les revendications territoriales globales et de leur incidence sur l'approvisionnement.

Title/Titre (Eng): Procurement in the Nunavut Settlement Area (COR410)
Description (English/anglais):
To fulfill its obligations under Article 24 of the Nunavut Agreement, the Government of Canada has issued the Directive on Government Contracts, Including Real Property Leases in the Nunavut Settlement Area, known as the "Nunavut Directive." This online self-paced course provides an overview of the Nunavut Directive and outlines the measures by which procurement specialists must provide fair and reasonable opportunities for Inuit firms to submit bids on government contracts. Participants will learn about the key policy measures of this directive and how to apply them during the procurement process. 

Topics include: 

· identifying when a procurement is subject to the Nunavut Directive 

· limiting bids to Inuit firms depending on market capacity (as per the Inuit Firm Registry) 

· including bid evaluation criteria related to benefits for Inuit and Nunavut, either on a best-effort or mandatory basis, depending on contract value 

· determining how to document and report on government contracts (as per the Nunavut Directive)
EN - Short description: This online self-paced course provides an overview of the Nunavut Directive and outlines the measures by which procurement specialists must provide fair and reasonable opportunities for Inuit firms to submit bids on government contracts.

The management of the federal government's extensive real property portfolio is based on a solid framework of legislation, regulations, policies, directives and guides. To support Canada's goal of reducing its greenhouse gas emissions, federal facilities have committed to taking practical steps to reduce energy consumption and carbon emissions from their operations. This online self-paced course provides an overview of the deep energy retrofit process and its adoption by federal organizations. ·      defining optimum performance
·      using technology applications for deep retrofits

This course has been adapted from training material for the United States Department of Energy's Federal Energy Management Program and is being delivered through Natural Resources Canada's Greening Government Services.

Description (English/anglais):
To carry out their responsibilities with respect to the public's right to information, federal employees who process requests for information are expected to have a solid understanding of the Access to Information Act and the Privacy Act. This course provides an overview of the proper handling of information and privacy requests, detailing the customary roles and responsibilities and how to apply the most common exemptions and exclusions. Participants will learn how to process access to information and privacy (ATIP) requests and provide valid recommendations on the disclosure of information.
 
 Topics include:
 
 • clarifying ATIP roles and responsibilities
 • applying exemptions and exclusions
 • providing rationales for recommendations
 • understanding ATIP-related jurisprudence

Title/Titre (Eng): Information Management in the Digital Age (COR506)
Description (English/anglais):
Canada, like most other countries, is experiencing a rapid transformation in the delivery of digital services and must keep pace with expectations. This course explains the roles of the information management (IM) community and the new program delivery techniques outlined in the Government of Canada's Digital Ambition. Through a blend of self-paced and virtual instructor-led learning, participants will explore the main trends influencing the field of information management and the IM activities that are supporting the government's transformation towards providing secure and modern digital services.

 

Topics include:

 

·         correlating IM trends and requirements with IM policy and strategic tools

·         conceptualizing a new information life cycle in the digital age

·         presenting a learning path for new IM professionals

·         exploring the IM knowledge and skills required in the workplace

 

Notes:

 

This course builds on the knowledge and skills acquired in Information Management in the Government of Canada (COR505) and focuses on applying information management in the digital age, as outlined in the Government of Canada's Digital Ambition.

Information Management in the Government of Canada (COR505) is a prerequisite.

Title/Titre (Eng): Cyber Security in the GC for Home and Telework (DDN232)
Description (English/anglais):
When working outside the secured work environment of a government office, employees are expected to take proactive measures to protect their work files from exposure to cyber threats. This online instructor-led course explores basic cyber security concepts and home network essentials, including system settings that can reduce online exposure to cyber security threats when teleworking. Participants will learn to apply the Communications Security Establishment's Top Ten IT Security Actions to protect information on their home network or mobile devices.

Topics include:

- updating system settings to reduce the exposure of private information
- storing sensitive information on a home network
- installing industry standard protective software
- adopting countermeasures to cyber security threats
- reacting to security breaches or incidents

Notes:

This course is delivered by the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security and has a cost of $750. To register and pay, or to sign in or create an account, visit the Cyber Centre Learning Hub and search for the course by title or by code CYB104C.

Upon request, this course can be tailored for groups to fit specific professional, business or departmental learning objectives. Email the Cyber Centre Learning Hub at education@cyber.gc.ca for specific details and costs.

Title/Titre (Eng): Online Privacy and Identity Management (DDN233)
Description (English/anglais):
Employees working in online environments face increased privacy and cyber security concerns stemming from both their professional and personal online activities. This course provides an overview of the online privacy landscape and recommends strategies for minimizing potential threats and managing one’s online identity. Participants will learn how to assess their digital footprint and identify best practices for managing and protecting their online identity.


Topics include:


·       increasing awareness of cyber security concerns linked to privacy

·       identifying tools and procedures to enhance digital privacy

·       providing a forward outlook on identity management


Notes:


This course is delivered by the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security and has a cost of $750. To register and pay, or to sign in or create an account, visit the Cyber Centre Learning Hub and search for the course by title or by code CYB103C.


Upon request, this course can be tailored for groups to fit specific professional, business or departmental learning objectives. Email the Cyber Centre Learning Hub at education@cyber.gc.ca.
EN - Short description: This course provides an overview of the cyber security landscape and the essentials of how to protect classified and sensitive information on Government of Canada networks. Participants will learn to assess their digital footprint and identify potential privacy threats associated with their online activities.
Title/Titre (Fra): La vie privée et la gestion de l'identité en ligne (DDN233)
Description (French/français):
Les employés qui travaillent en ligne éprouvent un nombre croissant de préoccupations liées à la protection de la vie privée et à la cybersécurité qui découlent auteur de leurs activités professionnelles que personnelles. Ce cours fournit un aperçu du paysage de la protection de la vie privée en ligne et propose des stratégies pour contrer les menaces et gérer son identité en ligne. Les participants apprendront à évaluer leur empreinte numérique et découvriront des pratiques exemplaires pour gérer et protéger leur identité en ligne.


Sujets traités :


·       apprendre à mieux connaître les préoccupations en matière de cybersécurité liées à la protection de la vie privée;

·       connaître les outils et les procédures visant à améliorer la protection des renseignements personnels numériques;

·       offrir des perspectives concernant la gestion de l’identité.


Remarques :


Ce cours est offert par le Centre canadien pour la cybersécurité au coût de 750 $. Pour vous inscrire au cours et le payer, ou pour ouvrir une session ou créer un compte, visitez le Carrefour de l'apprentissage du Centre pour la cybersécurité et faites une recherche en utilisant le titre du cours ou le code CYB103C.


Sur demande, ce cours peut être adapté à des groupes en fonction de leurs objectifs d'apprentissage professionnels ou encore de ceux de leur entreprise ou de leur ministère. Pour obtenir plus de renseignements sur ce service et sur ses coûts, écrivez au Carrefour de l'apprentissage du Centre pour la cybersécurité, à education@cyber.gc.ca.

Title/Titre (Eng): Discover Cyber Security (DDN235)
Description (English/anglais):
Digital technologies have quickly become an integral part of our daily lives, with new developments and security concerns emerging every day. This online self-paced course helps to build a greater awareness and understanding of the reality of cyber risks by exploring common security vulnerabilities and cyber threats, such as malware, password attacks and social engineering. Participants will learn to recognize potential threats and how to protect themselves, their digital information and the systems they use.

Topics include:

· defining cyber security and its importance

· protecting against malware and other cyber threats

· understanding Government of Canada security roles and policies

· adopting best practices

· pursuing additional security training opportunities

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for employees of the core public administration.

Learners will receive a certificate of completion after successfully completing the final quiz. Revalidation is required annually by completing Cyber Security Quest (DDN247) (recommended) or by redoing DDN235.

This course is offered in collaboration with the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security.
